# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code (claude.ai/code) and other contributors working in this repository. Internal notes for Globetrotters' own sessions live in an untracked `CLAUDE.local.md`, which is never committed or published.

## Commands

```bash
make install            # composer update --prefer-dist (this is a library: composer.lock is gitignored)
make test               # full phpunit suite
make test-unit          # tests/Unit only
make test-integration   # tests/Integration only (boots tests/Fixtures/TestKernel.php)
make stan               # phpstan, level 8, src/ only
make cs                 # php-cs-fixer check --diff
make cs-fix             # php-cs-fixer fix
make ci                 # cs + stan + test, the same gates CI runs
make release VERSION=x.y.z  # tag vX.Y.Z and push it (needs a ## [x.y.z] CHANGELOG section)
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, also called by `release.yml`) has a `lint` job (php-cs-fixer + phpstan on PHP 8.3), a `secrets` job (gitleaks over the full history, allowlist in `.gitleaks.toml`) and a `tests` matrix of PHP 8.2/8.3/8.4 crossed with Symfony 6.4.*/7.4.*, pinned via `SYMFONY_REQUIRE` and flex. A change that only passes on one Symfony major will fail the matrix, so check both branches when touching anything version-sensitive.

Style is `@Symfony` + `@Symfony:risky` + `declare_strict_types`, applied to `src/`, `config/` and `tests/`. Run `make cs-fix` before committing rather than hand-formatting.

## Architecture

A Symfony bundle (`globetrotters-ai/symfony-bundle` on Packagist) that serves a site's Official AI Presence at its **apex domain**. It pulls the published artefact set from the customer's Globetrotters subdomain on a schedule, caches it in a PSR-6 pool, and serves it. It is the Symfony counterpart of the [WordPress plugin](https://github.com/globetrotters-ai/gt-wordpress-plugin), and the two stay behaviourally aligned.

Namespace is `Globetrotters\AiPresenceBundle\` (PSR-4 from `src/`). The config key and extension alias are `globetrotters_ai_presence`, derived from the bundle class name.

`src/GlobetrottersAiPresenceBundle.php` is the composition root: it holds the whole config tree (an `AbstractBundle`, so no separate `Extension`/`Configuration` classes) and delegates service wiring to `config/services.php`, `config/analytics.php`, `config/scheduler.php` and `config/twig.php`.

Module map:

| Directory | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/Serving/` | The request path: `Router` plus the response/terminate subscribers, the locally generated `Sitemap` and `ApiCatalog`, and the page-view beacon (`PageViewBeacon` script, `PageViewEndpoint`, `PageViewBeaconInjector`) |
| `src/Client/`, `src/Sync/`, `src/Cache/` | Pull artefacts from the subdomain, validate, cache; the bundle's own pool (`SharedFilesystemAdapter`), the build-time pool guard (`CachePoolGuardPass`), the refresh lock and the `pulled_by` provenance |
| `src/Analytics/` | Agent-traffic reporting: NDJSON buffer, flush gate, ingest client; the page-view counter's store (`PageViewCounter`), path/UA rules and options; and the lists synced from the ranges document: vendor IP ranges (`VendorRanges`), AI referrers (`AiReferrers`), the AI crawler registry (`AiUserAgents`) |
| `src/Command/` | `gt:refresh`, `gt:status`, `gt:presence:flush` |
| `src/Scheduler/` | `symfony/scheduler` alternative to cron for refresh and flush |
| `src/Twig/` | `gt_ai_presence_head()` for explicit JSON-LD placement, the breadcrumb halves, and `gt_ai_presence_beacon()` for the page-view script |

### Request lifecycle

Ordering is load-bearing and every priority below is a deliberate choice, not a default:

| Event | Class | Priority | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kernel.request` | `Serving\Router` | 64 | Ahead of `RouterListener` (32) and the security firewall (8) so a catch-all controller or security bundle cannot claim the artefact paths; behind `ValidateRequestListener` (256) so trusted-host validation still runs |
| `kernel.request` | `Serving\PageViewEndpoint` | 64 | Same slot and reasons as `Router`, as a sibling so the artefact surface stays GET/HEAD-only; answering before the firewall is also what keeps a session (and its cookie) from starting. Always answers `POST /.well-known/globetrotters/pv` with an empty `204` while the bundle is installed (pages cached with the script keep beaconing after the counter is switched off); counts only when `reporting.page_views.enabled` and reporting are configured |
| `kernel.response` | `Serving\HeadInjector` | -10 | Injects server-rendered JSON-LD into the homepage HTML |
| `kernel.response` | `Serving\PageViewBeaconInjector` | -10 | Only with `page_views.auto_inject`, only on a `200`: inserts the beacon script before the last `</body>`; beside the other body rewriters so `ConditionalGetSubscriber` (-64) revalidates the final bytes |
| `kernel.response` | `Serving\RobotsFilter::captureHeadRepresentation` | 1 | Keeps a `HEAD` body before `ResponseListener` (0) empties it, so the `HEAD` can carry the decorated `GET`'s `ETag` and `Content-Length` |
| `kernel.response` | `Serving\RobotsFilter` | -20 | Decorates or generates `/robots.txt`; after `CacheAttributeListener` (-10) so late validators are dropped, before `ConditionalGetSubscriber` (-64) so it revalidates the final tag |
| `kernel.response` | `Serving\ArtefactHeaderSubscriber` | -1024 | Runs *last* on purpose, so it re-asserts `Router::NO_STORE_HEADERS` after anything downstream has had its chance to rewrite them — and strips every cookie from a page-view beacon response, below `SessionListener` (-1000) |
| `kernel.terminate` | `Serving\ArtefactCaptureSubscriber` | 0 | Records the served request, after the response is sent |
| `kernel.terminate` | `Serving\ServedVersionSubscriber` | 0 | Homepage and served-artefact GET/HEAD only, on every install (reporting or not): writes the bundle version this request read, with host, project dir, env and user, to `buffer_dir/served-version.json` (`Analytics\ServedVersion`) when it changed or every 5 minutes. The cross-check against `pulled_by` in `gt:status`, and `captureContext.servedVersion` |
| `kernel.terminate` | `Serving\SiteCaptureSubscriber` | 0 | Site bot capture (`Analytics\SiteCapture`): unmarked main requests only (not `ATTRIBUTE_PATH`/`KEY`/`SITEMAP`/`PAGE_VIEW`), GET/HEAD, `text/html`, coarse UA gate; writes a site line (no IP) to the shared buffer and notes CDN markers for `Analytics\CaptureContext`. Never triggers a flush |
| `kernel.terminate` | `Serving\OpportunisticFlushSubscriber` | -256 | Flushes after the capture above, at most every 15 min, for hosts with no cron and no Messenger worker — only on a served artefact request (`ATTRIBUTE_PATH`) or a page-view beacon (`ATTRIBUTE_PAGE_VIEW`, only while the counter is active), with events buffered or a closed page-view day waiting, and only where `Serving\ResponseFinalization` says the response was already delivered |

`Router` sets the response and stops propagation. A path miss or cold cache returns without touching the response so the app handles the request normally. Requests it serves are tagged with `Router::ATTRIBUTE_PATH` / `ATTRIBUTE_BYTES`, which is how the two later subscribers recognise them, so those attribute constants are an internal contract between four files. `PageViewEndpoint` sets `ATTRIBUTE_PAGE_VIEW` the same way for the header and terminate subscribers.

### The IndexNow key

`Router` answers one path that is not in `ContentTypes::MAP`, because its name is only known at runtime: the IndexNow key file at `/<key>.txt`. IndexNow verifies control of a host by reading it and comparing the body to the key, and the file must sit at the apex **root** — a key under `/.well-known/` scopes submissions to that directory and would cover none of the artefacts. The apex is served by the integrator's own stack, so nothing Globetrotters hosts can supply it there; without this route a file-drop apex cannot be announced at all.

The key rides on the version marker (`Sync\ArtefactSync::resolveVersionMarker` → `Options` state `indexnow_key`). It is not a required fetched path: adding it to `requiredPaths()` would 404 in every keyless environment and abort *every* sync there. It is not a bundle file either: the marker is injected after hashing, so the key cannot perturb `contentHash` or trip drift detection. `Serving\IndexNowKey` applies the backend's own key grammar (`[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,128}`) on the way in and on the way out — the marker arrives from `website_url`, which is untrusted input.

A served key is tagged with `Router::ATTRIBUTE_KEY`, deliberately **not** `ATTRIBUTE_PATH`: `ArtefactHeaderSubscriber` re-asserts the no-store headers for it, while `ArtefactCaptureSubscriber` — which keys off `ATTRIBUTE_PATH` — never sees it.

Rotation carries a lag this lane cannot avoid: a rotated key reaches an install only on its next refresh (daily by default), and submissions for that host fail verification during the window. Documented, not engineered around.

## Invariants worth preserving

- **The cache pool is shared by the CLI and the web, or the build fails.** The default `cache_pool` is the bundle's own `globetrotters_ai_presence.cache` (`Cache\SharedFilesystemAdapter`, `%kernel.project_dir%/var/globetrotters-ai-presence/cache`): outside `var/cache`, not tagged `cache.pool` (so `cache:clear` never empties it and its namespace never moves with the build), directories `2770` and files `0660` through a umask held around its writes — except on ZTS, where the umask is process-wide. `Cache\CachePoolGuardPass` (before removing, so parents and decorators are resolved) refuses an APCu, array, `cache.system` pool, or a wrapper with one inside: those are process-private, so a cron refresh succeeds and the apex keeps serving the old bundle (fixed in 0.9.4). `tests/Integration/SharedCachePoolTest.php` refreshes from a second kernel and serves from the first.
- **`servedVersion` is the web's word, never the CLI's.** It lives in `buffer_dir` (`served-version.json`), not in the pool it exists to cross-check, and `captureContext.servedVersion` (the version marker id, or null) reads it — a cron flush must report what the apex serves, not what the cron pulled. The ingest backend consumes that exact key and format; do not rename it. `gt:status` flags a mismatch only when the web observation is later than `pulled_by.at` (earlier is lag); the 5-minute heartbeat bounds how late. A trigger on the pool's own `pulled_by` would not work: a pool the web does not share never holds the CLI's stamp.
- **A refresh failure is recorded outside the pool.** `Sync\RefreshFailure` writes `buffer_dir/refresh-error.json` (message, version attempted, provenance) on every failed run, cleared by the next success; `last_error` in the pool state is still written, but it is lost exactly when the pool refused the write. The bundle pool's logger (`Cache\PoolFailureLog`) keeps the adapter's own reason for the message.
- **The 0.9.3 pool is a read-only fallback, and only for the default config.** With `cache_pool` left at its default, `Cache\LegacyPool` (a lazy, exception-swallowing `service_closure('cache.app')`) is read by `ArtefactCache` and `Options` while the bundle pool holds no manifest / no state item, and only for a bundle from this install's source. It is never written, may be APCu (the build guard is for the configured pool only), and makes `ArtefactSync::isDue()` true so the first refresh fills the real pool.
- **One refresh at a time per host.** `Sync\RefreshLock` (`buffer_dir/refresh.lock`, non-blocking `flock`) wraps the due-check and the pull in both `gt:refresh` and `RefreshMessageHandler`; a held lock is a clean skip (exit 0), an unusable directory runs unlocked rather than block the refresh.
- **Stale-serve.** The cached bundle is only ever replaced by a *fully successful* pull. A partial or failed refresh must leave the last known good version serving. "Successful" includes every JSON artefact parsing to an object (JSON-LD: or a list of node objects) — a `200` maintenance page is a failure. Keep that check shape-only; a field-level schema here would reject legitimate publications. `tests/Integration/RefreshStaleServeTest.php` guards this.
- **A bundle is served only for the `website_url` it was pulled from.** Stale-serve is for the *same* source failing; a bundle from another source is never a fallback. `ArtefactCache` stamps the normalized source into the manifest on `store()`, and its one read gate (`manifest()`) refuses a bundle from another source, or any bundle once `website_url` is cleared, so every reader — router, head injection, breadcrumb, sitemap, Twig, robots — is covered at once. The config changes with a deploy while the pool may outlive it, and serving cannot write, so the refresh is what clears it: `ArtefactSync::forgetForeignBundle()`, called by `run()` and, before its due-check, by `gt:refresh`, drops the bundle and resets the state learned from it, as the WordPress plugin does on a settings save — but only in a process that is itself connected. A CLI or worker with no `website_url` is as likely a missing env var as a withdrawn presence, and forgetting there would let it delete the bundle a correctly configured web tier serves. A manifest from 0.4.0 or earlier carries no stamp and stays servable while connected, so an upgrade does not go dark.
- **The flush interval is decided under the flush lock.** `Flusher::run()` checks `FlushGate::isDue()` inside `withLock()`, for every lane; a caller's own pre-check is only a cheap early exit. `--force` bypasses the interval, never the lock. The Scheduler polls every 5 minutes rather than every 15 so trigger jitter cannot make it skip alternate flushes.
- **The refresh is polled, never scheduled at its interval.** The Scheduler asks hourly and `RefreshMessageHandler` pulls only when `ArtefactSync::isDue()` says `refresh_interval` has elapsed — the check `gt:refresh` applies under cron. A periodical trigger first fires one period after the worker starts and its checkpoint dies with the pool, so a trigger at the interval itself would leave a cache emptied by a deploy dark for a day or a week.
- **Serving needs no filesystem write access.** Only reporting writes (to `reporting.buffer_dir`), plus one diagnostic: the served-version heartbeat, written on `kernel.terminate` after the response, on every install, and silently skipped when the directory is not writable. Do not introduce a write on the response path. The page-view counter endpoint is reporting, not serving: it writes only to `buffer_dir`, only when opted in, and an unwritable directory costs the count, never the `204`.
- **`buffer_dir` is shared between OS users.** The web user and the flush's user are often different accounts in one group. `BufferDirectory` creates the directory `2770` (setgid) and every writer gives a file it *creates* `0660` via `share()` — explicitly, because the umask would leave it `0644` — and never re-chmods an existing one. Anything that only reads through its handle and replaces by `rename()` opens via `openForLock()`, which falls back to read-only (`flock()` needs no write access, `rename()`/`unlink()` need only the directory). Never `touch()` a shared file with an explicit time: that needs ownership; `FlushGate::stamp()` renames a fresh file over the stamp instead. Nothing is world-readable: the event log holds client IPs.
- **The page-view counter never reads an IP, never stores the User-Agent, never sets a cookie.** `PageViewEndpoint` must not call `getClientIp()`/`ClientIpResolver`; it keeps a coarse bucket, not the UA string; and `ArtefactHeaderSubscriber` strips cookies the host app adds to its response. `PageViewEndpointTest` traps any IP read and inspects what is written; `tests/Integration/PageViewCounterTest.php` asserts no `Set-Cookie` against an app that stamps one on every response. The script (`PageViewBeacon::SCRIPT`) posts only to a root-relative same-origin path, and is byte-identical to the WordPress plugin's — both repos pin the same literal in `PageViewBeaconTest`, so change both together.
- **A page view keeps the referring platform, never the referrer.** The beacon sends `r` (the referrer host) and `u` (`utm_source`); `PageViewEndpoint` hands them to `AiReferrers::match()` for a `browser` view only and keeps the platform slug it returns (`none` when unmatched, the list is missing, or it is older than 14 days). `u` is cut at its first `?` and looked up only when `r` is empty or matches none of the list's `searchHosts` patterns; a document without that key reads as an empty list; a stored file without it (0.10.x) matches as one too, but `AiReferrers::version()` returns null for it, so the next sync sends no `If-None-Match` — 0.10.x may hold the list at the very ranges version that introduced the key, and a `304` would keep the old shape until the backend's version moved. A restamp never adds the key. Neither value is written, logged or sent: `PageViewEndpointTest` and `tests/Integration/PageViewCounterTest.php` assert no counter file holds `chatgpt.com` or `utm_source`. The match reads only `buffer_dir/ai-referrers.json`, and only when `r` or `u` is non-empty; `AiReferrers` depends on the directory and the clock alone, and the endpoint never takes `VendorRanges` — `PageViewEndpointTest` proves both through a recording stream wrapper (`tests/Support/OpenRecordingStream.php`). The counter key stays `"bucket\tpath"` for `none` — byte-identical to 0.8.x, so an open day survives the upgrade — and is `"bucket@platform\tpath"` otherwise; the path cap counts paths, so a path's platform rows fold together. Kept in step with the WordPress plugin.
- **One ranges document, three files, one version.** `VendorRanges::refresh()` fetches `<ingest endpoint>/ranges` daily with the ingest token and writes `vendor-ranges.json`, `ai-referrers.json` and `ai-user-agents.json` in `buffer_dir`; a `200` replaces all three (a document without a list stores it empty), a `304` re-stamps them, anything else keeps them. It sends `If-None-Match` only when all three files hold the same version, so an upgrade that adds a file makes the first fetch unconditional rather than let a `304` keep the new list from arriving.
- **Page-view ids are minted once, at sealing.** `Flusher::run()` seals every closed UTC day under the flush lock (`PageViewCounter::seal()`), which is the only place a record gets its UUID — idempotently: each sealed record stores a `src` fingerprint of its open file (the random generation written into it at creation — not the inode, which Linux reuses at once), so an open file that survived a crash after its sealed file was written is unlinked, not re-sealed, and `src` is never sent; records are deleted only after a 2xx, so a retry re-sends the same ids and the backend dedupes. Today is never sent, and days older than the backend's 7-day window are pruned, not sent. Page views must never depend on agent traffic: every lane flushes them with an empty event buffer. With `page_views.enabled` off, `Flusher` neither seals nor sends them and deletes nothing but days past the 7-day window: a CLI or worker missing the flag must not destroy the web tier's counts.
- **An increment never blocks.** `PageViewCounter::increment()` takes the day's lock with `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` (10 tries, 5 ms apart) and drops the view rather than queue FPM workers; it writes a temp file and `rename()`s it over the open file while holding the old inode's lock, so a killed write cannot truncate a day, and a waiter holding the replaced inode sees `nlink == 0` and retries on the new file. This needs `buffer_dir` on a local POSIX filesystem.
- **A site event never carries an IP.** `Event::site()` has no IP parameter, the buffered line has no `ip` key, and `Flusher` sends site lines under `siteEvents`. `SiteCapture` resolves the IP only to match it in memory against `VendorRanges` and keeps `verified` + `vendor`. Kept in step with the WordPress plugin.

It is fetched through `NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient` (wired in `config/services.php`) so a configured URL cannot be pointed at a private or reserved IP, including across redirects. Keep any new outbound fetch on that client, not on raw `http_client`.
- **The ingest endpoint is https-only, at three layers.** It receives the bearer token and every captured client IP. The config tree refuses a literal non-https `reporting.endpoint` at build; `AnalyticsOptions::endpoint()` reads one as `''` (unconfigured) at runtime, which is the layer that holds for the documented `%env()%` binding, since the build only ever sees its placeholder; and `IngestClient::post()` refuses before sending, with an error that never carries the token. - **The key is served only when one is stored, and only at its own URL.** No stored key means the path falls through to the application's normal 404 — never a 200 with an empty body, which would answer a verification fetch with a file that fails it. `ArtefactSync` writes `indexnow_key` on every *successful* pull including a keyless one, so a key rotated away upstream stops being served rather than lingering; a failed pull writes nothing, so the last known key keeps serving alongside the last known good bundle. - **Serving the key is not agent traffic.** Presence Analytics counts agent fetches of the artefact set; a search engine reading the key to verify host control is neither, and folding it in would inflate the numbers a customer reads as demand for their presence.

Refreshes run daily whether or not anything moved; stamping URLs with the refresh date claims a freshness the content does not have. `ArtefactSync` writes it only when the content hash changes. It is never a fallback source, `0` omits `<lastmod>`, and the homepage is never stamped — it is the customer's page, not ours to date. Matches the WordPress plugin.

Every `ContentTypes::MAP` entry except the marker is a required artefact of a refresh (the marker is fetched on its own and synthesized when missing), and the server-log ingest must map every served path, or its captured hits are dropped. Homepage only, `200` HTML only, only the targets this install serves (a cached artefact, or the catalog once one of its targets is cached), and added as its own header line so an app's `Link` header (WebLink) survives.

## Releasing

The version lives in three places that must move together: `GlobetrottersAiPresenceBundle::VERSION`, the `CHANGELOG.md` heading, and the `extra.branch-alias.dev-main` constraint in `composer.json`. Packagist publishes from the git tag, so tag only after all three agree. Tagging is `make release VERSION=x.y.z` on an up-to-date `main` once the bump is merged: it refuses without a `## [x.y.z]` CHANGELOG section or when the tag exists, then pushes `vX.Y.Z`. The number is kept in step with the WordPress plugin so the same behaviour ships under the same version on both.

`.gitattributes` keeps the Packagist dist to what a consumer needs: tests, tooling and both `CLAUDE*.md` files are `export-ignore`. Check with `git archive HEAD | tar -t` after touching it.

Issues are welcome; pull requests are by invitation — see `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Report vulnerabilities privately as `SECURITY.md` describes, never in a public issue.

name: Release

# Tag-triggered release. Checks that CHANGELOG.md has a section for the tag and
# that the version agrees with the code, runs the full CI matrix, and cuts a
# GitHub Release with that CHANGELOG section as its notes. Packagist publishes
# from the tag itself, so this workflow does not touch it: the Release is for
# provenance and readable notes. `make release VERSION=x.y.z` pushes the tag.

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  changelog:
    name: Check version & extract notes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Verify version consistency
        run: |
          VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          if ! echo "$VERSION" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$'; then
            echo "::error::Tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME is not vX.Y.Z."
            exit 1
          fi
          CONST=$(grep -oE "const VERSION = '[^']+'" src/GlobetrottersAiPresenceBundle.php | grep -oE "[0-9][^']*")
          ALIAS=$(grep -oE '"dev-main": "[^"]+"' composer.json | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')
          echo "tag=$VERSION const=$CONST branch-alias=$ALIAS.x-dev"
          if [ "$VERSION" != "$CONST" ] || [ "${VERSION%.*}" != "$ALIAS" ]; then
            echo "::error::Version drift — tag=$VERSION const=$CONST branch-alias=$ALIAS.x-dev must agree."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Extract CHANGELOG section
        run: |
          VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          if ! grep -q "^## \[$(echo "$VERSION" | sed 's/\./\\./g')\]" CHANGELOG.md; then
            echo "::error::CHANGELOG.md has no '## [$VERSION]' section."
            exit 1
          fi
          # The lines after the heading, up to the next '## [' heading, without
          # leading or trailing blank lines or link reference definitions.
          awk -v h="## [$VERSION]" '
            index($0, h) == 1 { on = 1; next }
            on && /^## \[/ { exit }
            on && /^\[[^]]+\]: / { next }
            on && /^[[:space:]]*$/ { if (started) blanks++; next }
            on { while (blanks > 0) { print ""; blanks-- } print; started = 1 }
          ' CHANGELOG.md > release-notes.md
          if [ ! -s release-notes.md ]; then
            echo "::error::CHANGELOG.md section '## [$VERSION]' is empty."
            exit 1
          fi
          cat release-notes.md

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: release-notes
          path: release-notes.md

  ci:
    name: CI
    needs: changelog
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  release:
    name: Publish GitHub Release
    needs: [changelog, ci]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-notes

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          name: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          body_path: release-notes.md
          make_latest: 'true'

- `console.log` / `debugger` statements

- Leftover test-only code

# Smart PR

## Trigger

Use when saying "create a PR", "open a PR", "pull request", or ready to open a PR after committing changes.

## Workflow

1. Check the current branch. If it is `main` (or `master`), do NOT commit or push there — create and switch to a new branch first (see Branch Safety below).
2. Check current branch state and ensure all changes are committed.
3. Review the full diff against the base branch to understand all changes.
4. Detect the sub-project and run its quality gates (lint, typecheck, tests).
5. Draft a PR title and description from the commit history and diff.
6. Push the branch and create the PR.
7. Request a GitHub Copilot code review on the newly created PR.

## Branch Safety

Never commit directly on the default branch. Detect it and bail out into a new branch if needed:
```bash
current=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$current" = "main" ] || [ "$current" = "master" ]; then
  # Create a new branch BEFORE committing. Name it from the change:
  # <type>/<short-slug> matching the conventional-commit type (feat, fix, refactor, …).
  git switch -c <type>/<short-slug>
fi
```
- Derive the branch name from the pending changes (e.g. `feat/product-catalog-page`, `fix/org-list-error`).
- If changes are already committed on `main`, move them onto a new branch before pushing (create the branch from HEAD, then reset `main` back if appropriate) and confirm with the user first.
- Once on a non-default branch, proceed normally.

### Worktrees

This skill may run inside a git worktree — Claude Code isolates a task under
`.claude/worktrees/<name>`, and other orchestration tools do the same. Detect it
and adjust:
```bash
# In a linked worktree the git dir and the common dir differ. This holds
# whatever created the worktree — prefer it over any vendor-specific env var.
[ "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" != "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" ] && in_worktree=1
```
- Never run `git worktree remove`, `git worktree prune`, delete, or otherwise clean up the current worktree — whatever created it owns its lifecycle.
- The worktree is typically already on its own task branch; only create a new branch if it is still on `main`/`master`.
- Do not switch the worktree back to `main` or reset it as part of cleanup.
- Run every command from the worktree path. Do not `cd` to the original repo root.

## Commands

```bash
git status
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
# If on main/master, create a branch first (see Branch Safety):
# git switch -c <type>/<short-slug>
git log --oneline main...HEAD
git diff main...HEAD --stat
# Run quality gates based on the sub-project detected from changed files.
# Check the sub-project's CLAUDE.md for the correct lint/typecheck/test commands.
# Skip gates that don't exist for the sub-project.
git push -u origin HEAD
gh pr create --title "<title>" --body "<body>"
# Request Copilot review — capture PR number from the URL returned above,
# or resolve it with: gh pr view --json number -q .number
gh pr edit <PR_NUMBER> --add-reviewer @copilot
```

## PR Title Format

Use the same conventional-commit format as the `dev-commit` skill:<type>(<scope>): <short summary>
- Under 70 characters.
- Scope is optional.
- Types: feat, fix, refactor, test, docs, chore, perf, ci, style, wip.
- Examples: `fix: show error page when org list fails to load`, `feat(dashboard): add product catalog page`.

## PR Body Format

```markdown
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points explaining what changed and why>
## Test plan
- [ ] <how to verify the changes>
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```
- If a PRD or issue is relevant, link it in the summary.
- If there are screenshots or visual changes, note where to check.

## Code Review Scan

Before opening the PR, check the full diff for:
- `console.log` / `debugger` statements
- TODO/FIXME/HACK comments without ticket references
- Hardcoded secrets, API keys, or credentials
- Leftover test-only code
- `.env` files or other sensitive config
Flag any issues before proceeding.

## Guardrails

- Never commit directly on `main`/`master` — always create a feature branch first.
- Never clean up or delete the current worktree — leave its lifecycle to the tool that created it.
- Never skip quality gates unless user explicitly says to.
- Never force push unless user explicitly asks.
- Always confirm the PR title and description with the user before creating.
- Ensure the branch is up to date with the base branch (warn if behind).
- Never open a PR with uncommitted changes — commit first.

- Quality gate results (pass/fail)
- Issues found in diff (if any)
- Suggested PR title and body (ask user to confirm or edit)
- PR URL after creation
- Confirmation that Copilot review was requested (run `/dev-fix-pr-copilot-review` once the review completes)

Review target: `main...HEAD`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
